This file is the canonical substance store for Project Io's weekly sprint rhythm — every
sprint's goal, planned items, retro (landed/slipped/runtime/feedback) and free-form notes
(rulings, audit tables, amendments, risk paragraphs) that don't fit the fixed fields.
SPRINTS.md itself is now a thin header: intro prose, the Format template, and a regenerated
compact status table pointing here.
FIELDS per entry in `sprints`:
id           — sprint number/label as used in prose (e.g. '19', '26a', '22-24 preamble').
theme        — short human handle for the sprint (pair with id in prose, same rule as BL ids).
state        — one of: open, closed, proposed, superseded, gated, subsumed, retro-recorded, landed.
opened_date / closed_date — ISO dates where recorded in the source prose; null where the
entry never carries an explicit date (many 'proposed' entries were never opened).
goal         — the sprint's stated (or reconstructed, for retro-recorded entries) goal.
planned      — array of planned items/work, one string per item, as close to source phrasing
as practical.
retro        — object with landed/slipped/filed/runtime/feedback string fields where the
source entry carries a closed retro. Omitted for sprints with no retro yet.
risk         — the sprint's stated risk paragraph(s), where present.
done_when    — the sprint's stated done-when criterion, where present.
notes        — catch-all prose: rulings, audit tables (rendered as markdown), amendments,
'what this sprint deliberately does not carry' sections, sequencing notes. This is where
almost all of the original file's density lives for the larger/proposal-style entries.
The 'Sprints 26-33: The Fall' arc (proposed 2026-08-18) is captured as one parent entry
(id '26-33', the full audit/shape/rulings/adversarial-pass prose) plus one entry per named
D1-D4) — the two that actually opened (26a, 26b) carry their own opened_date and status-table
row; the rest stay 'proposed' pending Ben's pick, per the source.
`status_table` mirrors the source file's 'Where things stand' index — id/theme/state only,
for a quick scan; the full prose for every row lives in `sprints` above.
Landed items referenced by BL-id here are NOT re-described — see backlog.json (or the cold
archive once landed) for that item's own design/resolution prose. This file is about the
sprint as a unit of pacing and sequencing, not a duplicate backlog.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22, same convention as backlog.json): a sprint entry may carry
an `author` field naming who is running it (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only; nullable;
missing/null means unattributed (the default dev-sprint rhythm).

sprints.theme: The release sprint
sprints.goal: No goal was stated at the start — the sprint rhythm had lapsed, and direction came from a live steer rather than a written goal. Ben, opening: "cut as many versions as we can now, rather than working on the lofty, conceptual stuff."

retro.landed: Five versions tagged — v0.1.1 (the word interface), v0.1.2 (buildings rework), v0.1.8 (build health), v0.1.9 (shell & legibility), v0.1.10 (generation & content) — against zero in the preceding six days. 24 backlog items closed; open items 97 → 77 despite 13 new items filed. Every cut minor now carries a done-definition, written at its cut — that was the structural fix, not the tags. The gate went from lying to green: had been reporting ten failures of which exactly one was a failing assertion; v0.1.8 re-tiered it, and v0.1.10 closed with 55 tests, 0 failures — the first fully green gate of the arc. Four stub minors stopped being design-only: BL-342-345 turn v0.1.3/v0.1.4/v0.1.6 into buildable work, on the finding that BL-155 and BL-156 had both settled on the same condition_set object and neither built it.
retro.feedback: Held: worktree sub-agents did the bulk of the work and several outperformed their briefs — one refused its own instructions because BL-216 §1-3 was superseded by a complete item and implementing it would have reverted a landed decision; another volunteered that a knife-edge test had influenced its parameter choice (BL-349). Did not hold: three of five agents in the v0.1.9 batch branched from a base that had already moved, and every one produced code that would not merge cleanly — worktrees isolate writes, not history. The v0.1.10 batch was worse: one agent's commit swallowed a whole fast-forward (328 files) and cost 36 conflicts to integrate. Integration read every hunk rather than trusting a clean auto-merge, and that is why the Ages view and the disclosure controls survived.

sprints.notes: Diagnosis before any work: 119 commits since the v0.1.0 tag and not one version cut, with CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] still reading "Nothing yet" — the changelog was not merely un-stamped, it was not accruing. Root cause (NR-103): the roadmap wrote done-definitions for exactly two versions, v0.1.0 and v1.0.0 — and those were the only two ever cut or scheduled. A theme with no done-definition has no test for finished, so it absorbs items indefinitely (v0.1.1 was the proof: its three theme legs shipped 2026-08-03, and 26 unrelated items were then retrofitted onto the same tag over the following week). Measurement overturned the stated cause four times: BL-338 wetland (story: relief commits displaced it; measured: refuted by rebuilding the audit at 802421c^ — identical census, wetland is a drainage feature and elevation had no vote in composition), BL-347 econ tick (story: an O(n log n) sort; measured: the sort was 3%, cost was std::map allocation in worlds with no stacks), BL-346 estimator (story: BL-079's reflex reads an inflated number; measured: retracted — that function reads realised credit, real site was the pre-build estimator), pan "lag" (story: needs a 200ms input delay; measured: panning costs nothing, static and panning measured identically — it was 157k vertices at whole-grid zoom). A green gate can lie: logistics_reach_harness failed three assertions from byte-identical sources — a conflict-heavy merge left ninja holding a stale object that touch would not dislodge. Standing lesson: --clean-first before cutting after a messy merge, and if a harness fails suspiciously, build the same commit in a throwaway worktree before believing it. Left for another session: v0.1.11 open with four items (generation globe BL-256, deed history lines BL-309, BL-348 province names half-native, BL-349); v0.1.3-v0.1.7 remain uncut and are next in sequence; 42 items still sit at post-v0.1.0 (NR-101's finding); Windows work owed (stale visual/MSVC goldens, BL-341 parked).

(2) NR-101 was the same finding at document level: twenty of the 45 unversioned items were already assigned by ROADMAP.md in prose (the whole v0.4.0 politics substrate, most of the v0.3.0 Era −1 arc) — the roadmap and the backlog disagreed, and the disagreement was invisible because the prose was not queryable and the query did not read prose. Sprint 6's lesson was measure before you fix; Sprint 7's is adjacent: before estimating a blocked thing, check whether anything is actually blocking it. The design test earned its keep concretely: BL-094 asks "does this system reach military as well as economic outcomes?" — it changed two decisions this sprint at no extra cost (condition_set shipped military_units/military_strength alongside six economic subjects; the tech gate went on the Military Base rather than a smelter). Two collisions between the sprint's own decisions, both caught by writing the assertion first: BL-342 established that an empty condition_set is true (common case for a law); BL-344 then needed the opposite for a tech (~130 authored nodes with no gate would have earned themselves on the first tick) — fixed with a separate earnable flag: absence has to be modelled by absence, not by an empty predicate. Second collision was structural: the predicate could not live in tech_tree.cpp, because that TU pulls in sol2 and is excluded from the world superset a harness links.

sprints.notes: Where the method held: by not doing the thing — Sprint 6's worst cost was worktree agents branching from a moved base (36 conflicts to integrate one commit); this sprint's three items were one dependency chain across ~2 files each, so built sequentially in the main session, stated as a call rather than defaulted into. The bench prediction paid off exactly: econ_stability and home_surface_bench failed at -j 4 and passed re-run idle, precisely as the v0.1.9 retro said they would (they assert absolute wall-clock, so they measure the machine). Where it did not hold: the JSON stores got corrupted three times — long resolution prose full of backticks (condition_set, apply_budget, earnable) inside a shell heredoc are command substitution, the shell silently deletes the word and mangled text lands in the canonical store looking almost right; three repair passes; fixed durably by writing edit scripts to a file and running them, saved to memory. The pacing signal is not being collected — third consecutive entry whose Runtime line reads "not tracked": tools/session/timer.js exists, the format block asks for the number explicitly, and nobody starts it; the commit span measures the landing, not the work. Left for another session: NR-115 (world generation places starting military bases through the tile-only check, so a corp can begin a campaign with a base it has not researched — defensible as fiction, a one-line fix either way); NR-102 (sequencing decoupling, now the standing structural item — a minor per item is not an order to build them in); v0.1.5/6/7 remain uncut, v0.1.11 now carries ten items (largest open minor); Windows work still owed.

retro.landed: BL-428 complete — recipe_required_depth + corporation_component::produced_ever + refusal at both construct_building and try_switch_recipe. 6 tasks, 4 requirements, all met. chain_depth gained 11 assertions (G1-G4), including BL-432's no-stranded-building row. retro.feedback: Every substantive finding came from measuring something, and four times the measurement overturned the plausible story (same pattern Sprint 11's retro recorded): "Keep only profitable player seeds" → profitability is NOT the discriminator, all 24 seeds end positive, none dip, 13/24 fail on having no processing facility. "The Method page overlap is a draw-order bug" → draw order was half of it, fixing only that gave "..."; the row was 160px holding 248px of content. "The app crashed after ~3s" → --autostart-windowed is a smoke test that exits by design at 120 frames. "The queue has 36 open entries" → it has 18, 15 open — the count had measured _note's lines. A gate on one door is not a gate: BL-428's design named placement as what depth gates, and implementing exactly that would have shipped a one-click bypass via retooling — worth generalising, when a rule is added to one seam, ask what the other routes to the same state are before calling it done. The check that had never actually run was hiding a live defect: building_management_shell.lua had been pointing at a deleted tab (NR-246) and still passing — capture-only, no golden, nothing comparing anything; its first honest photograph immediately showed the Method page's two load-bearing numbers printed on top of each other. A check that runs green while looking at the wrong thing is worse than no check, because it is counted as coverage. A stale tool doc costs a session's first hour: the verifier-headless vcvars path had been wrong since 2026-07-28 and failed on the first translation unit every time; corrected, symptom quoted so the next person recognises it in one read.

sprints.notes:
This is a proposal, not a decision, and it is a resumption not a pivot: BL-299 (great-power seed) was filed 2026-08-04 at Ben's own request and already says two majors with opposed creeds in a multipolar antiquity, 'while the focus is on how these empires change and crumble' — what is missing is the crumble. Does not contradict the non-hegemony invariant: BL-224 asserts no world-conquering nation as a cross-seed tuning target, and BL-299 already reconciles them ('neither major absorbs the world early; the periphery stays alive as actors, not terrain'). THE AUDIT — ten read-only slices, 2026-08-18, run as a ten-agent fan-out over src/ and the doc corpus, evidence file:line not doc claim. Five findings that reshape the plan: (1) the sim's political result is discarded before the campaign starts — generate_nations seeds one nation per province anchor with no reference to polity ownership, a perfect rise-and-fall leaves NO trace at 0 CE (hard_coded_world.cpp:56, settlement.cpp:498-505). (2) there is no collapse mechanic of any kind — no secession, succession crisis, revolt, civil war or dissolution; territory moves only by conquest, owner_none never emitted, alive=false is silent (history_sim.cpp:466,:1198). (3) the two hegemons exist in code and are switched off — seed_great_powers defaults false, polity::major written and read NOWHERE in src/ (history_sim.hpp:371, history_sim.cpp:290-291). (4) zero trade routes exist structurally — trade_route keyed on a body PAIR and supply_system.cpp:65 skips lanes where source and destination bodies match, always true on a one-planet arc (components.hpp, supply_system.cpp:58-65). (5) a tech cannot express a buff — the whole effect vocabulary is one field, building_type unlocks_structure; the condition side has 9 subjects and 5 comparators, a 9:1 asymmetry (tech_gate.hpp:53, condition_set.hpp:47-77). The capability table (30 rows) covers: Era −1 sim BUILT; two-great-power seeding BUILT-OFF; conquest transferring a province DEFECT (BL-384: 267 battles, 0 conquests); collapse/secession/fragmentation ABSENT; hegemony measure ABSENT (only a reporting threshold); sim steppable/pausable ABSENT; per-year decision trace ABSENT; polity-pair state ABSENT; nation-grain blackboard ABSENT; Ages view BUILT but shows the wrong history; campaign hostility/stance model ABSENT (stance.* doesn't exist); a verb naming a live unit ABSENT (17 corp_verbs, none takes a unit subject); unit upkeep/ordnance/supply decay BUILT-RATE-ZERO; corp-to-corp trade ABSENT; order-book matching DEAD CODE; nation treasury/tariff/customs ABSENT; law with author/scope ABSENT; law enactment DEFECT (a corporation flips world law via a debug checkbox); wage as a lever ABSENT; tech effect kinds PARTIAL (1 of 132 techs earnable); roads crossing water ABSENT; roads for <2 centres ABSENT; a drawn surface trade lane ABSENT; nation capital carried to campaign DEFECT; corporation KIND axis ABSENT; developed-tile representation ABSENT; world build density 0.2-0.5% (~55-150 buildings, 31 centres, 31,581 tiles). Two corrections the audit forces: '0 AD' is the YEAR (settled twice, NR-060) — the RTS was installed and retired the same day, the arena is Io's own sandbox; and the backlog's status cannot be trusted — ~15 items whose code is in src/ still read designed (BL-452, BL-453 among them). THE SHAPE — one serial spine, three parallel lanes: the collapse is a generation outcome so its spine is serial (nothing can collapse before conquest works, nothing can inherit a border before the map is inherited, nothing can be watched before it is retained); everything else runs alongside. Lane A — the spine (conquest, inheritance, hegemony, collapse, the watch): history_sim.*, combat.cpp, settlement.cpp, hard_coded_world.cpp. Lane B — the civilised world (capitals, roads, ports, land/sea lanes, density, corp kind): road_generation.*, population_generation.*, supply_system.*, logistics.*, corporation_generation.*. Lane C — force and stance (stance, the unit verb, the engagement trigger, live upkeep): stance.* (new), corp_command.*, campaign_battle.*, economy.lua. Lane D — tech meta, law, and the nation as an actor (the effect union, modifier vocabulary, author/scope, treasury, tax, wages, tariffs): tech_gate.*, law.*, budget_system.*, condition_set.*, components.hpp. Two collisions named rather than discovered: Lane A's inheritance sprint and Lane B's settlement-density work both touch settlement.cpp; Lanes C and D both append to condition_subject in condition_set.hpp (an append-only serialised enum — one appender per batch); worktree isolation covers writes, sequencing note stops a semantic conflict. Sequencing and supersession: Sprints 21/23/25b superseded by Lane C explicitly — Sprint 23 becomes C1, Sprint 21 becomes C2+C3, 25b sits after C1 and C3; this resolves the unreconciled ordering contradiction (NR-312 settled 25a→21→23→25b while Sprint 23's own block said it must precede 21) — Lane C runs stance first. Sprint 22 (reachability) survives untouched, good filler for any lane finishing short. FIVE AMENDMENTS from the candidate-plan pass (three independent plans — substrate-first, seam-first, playable-first — judged adversarially, converged on this shape): (1) decide the relationship idiom ONCE, in the sim — Lane A's collapse needs polity-pair state, Lane C needs corp-pair stance, both the same question (directed map or canonicalised pair); settle it in Sprint 30 and have Lane C consume it. (2) Era −1 tech state dies at the handoff too — polity::capacity[7] discarded alongside borders; under ruling 2 (borders plus character) it should ride the same crossing, add to Sprint 29's payload. (3) the campaign roster band is hard-coded to INDUSTRIAL (unit_roster.hpp:61) while default epoch is 0 CE — cheap, embarrassing, Lane C's natural home (this became BL-461 in Sprint C1). (4) markets are era-blind — base_price, background demand basket and population basket ungated by era; Lane B, alongside density work. (5) the economy-truth arc is carried, not dropped — Sprint 19 closed unmet, ai_skill_harness reads -1.9M to -3.4M final net worth on every seed; Lane D's tax/wage work measured against that benchmark; BL-443 (debt floor) is the cheapest unblock (interest is 98.8% of every benchmark deficit) and should ride inside Lane D's first sprint. And one honest gap all three plans flagged: there is no serialiser — no save/load path exists anywhere, only BL-107's format header filed; ruling 2 makes Sprint 29 the first work whose loss on reload actually matters (does not block the arc, the collapse stays re-derivable from seed plus params, but it is the moment the project stops being able to defer it). THE ADVERSARIAL PASS — nine corrections (three judges: dependency realism, determinism/standing rules, scope honesty, instructed to default to finding the flaw): (1) the strain accumulator must be asserted on its SHAPE not its value — the burden of breadth (history_sim.cpp:507-524) is STATELESS, burden=(held-40)×4, recomputed each round from the CURRENT holding count, so losing provinces immediately REDUCES the burden — shrinking makes an empire logistically stronger, a negative feedback actively opposing collapse; Sprint 30's harness must assert the strain term does not decrease when holdings decrease. (2) BL-317's timelapse is a data race not a plumbing job — app.cpp:440 runs make_hard_coded_world under std::async, reading owner_changes mid-generation is an unsynchronised read of a vector the worker is appending to; Sprint 31 must publish per-year snapshots through a synchronised channel or replay only after the join (ruling 1 makes the second legal and cheap). The item's headline case would have shipped INERT and looked implemented. Measuring the new behaviour, not just the regression, is what caught it (NR-446).

2. A REFACTOR CAN BE MADE FALSIFIABLE, and it is worth the structure. BL-519 was 522 references across ~110 files. It was landable in one pass because Pass 4a's RNG consumption was held identical draw-for-draw and both new passes consume no stream at all — so the claim 'nothing drifted' could be tested rather than asserted. The 120-seed earthlike census came back BIT-IDENTICAL, and that one measurement is what made every other moved number attributable. Carry this: when a refactor touches a seeded pipeline, the cheap thing is to keep the stream fixed and let a census prove it.

3. THE CEILING RULING GENERALISED IMMEDIATELY. NR-438's shape — a stated number becomes a PREFERENCE, a real bound is ASSERTED, and the over-share is REPORTED because 'rare' was never defined — was reused within hours by BL-516's sea provinces, which hit exactly the same wall at 82 against 'say 80' (NR-460). A ruling that produces a reusable discipline is worth more than one that produces a number.

4. THE FAN-OUT COST AN HOUR, and the cause is filed (NR-459). Three agents ran concurrently; all three got worktrees at the SESSION's base rather than at HEAD. One fast-forwarded itself, one did not and built an entire item against the enum BL-519 had just deleted. The port was cheap only because that agent had routed every water test through one choke-point predicate. Two agents also independently minted the same review ids, because NEEDS_REVIEW.json has no next_id.js. Both are process fixes, not judgement failures.

WHAT IS OWED, and it is the honest weakness of the whole arc: NOTHING WAS RENDERED. Four of the six items have a UI half, and the session ran in a container that cannot build the GUI. Everything is compile-clean against real ImGui headers and arithmetically checked; none of it has been seen. No golden was blessed, because blessing an unseen frame pins whatever got built. For a sprint whose own method note is 'build it, look at it, then rule', ending without the looking is the thing to fix — and BL-521, built this same session, is what makes the looking cheap next time.

CARRIED FORWARD: BL-518 (the Era -1 sim redrawing borders as its wars resolve) is the last clause of Ben's brief and is still design-owed with three undecided questions. BL-514 (blend all tiles) stays HELD, and BL-520 has now given it a second reason to be decided — texture and the blend are in direct tension.

**Goal met, but not on the first pass, and the second pass is the finding.**

All three subsystems landed and all three land INERT, as designed: `nation_budget.{hpp,cpp}`, `sentiment.{hpp,cpp}` and the `value_anchor` check are in the build, three new harnesses are green (36 / 41 / 22), and a world runs bit-identical to the pre-sprint build because nothing calls any of them. **What it cost to get there: three agents wrote the code AND its harness, all three harnesses passed — 17/17, 39/39, 25/25 — and two of the three subjects were unsound.** The adversarial pass found a heap-buffer-overflow (a `uint8_t`-backed enum indexing a 9-element array, ASan-confirmed), an overdrawable treasury, a conservation claim carried entirely by a dyadic fixture, a check that went RED on the day its subject was satisfied, a content claim that survived a x10 reprice, and an order-independence row that survived deleting the sort it guarded.

**Not one of those was found by reading.** They were found by mutating the content the check reads, mutating the code the check guards, generating shapes instead of authoring one, and turning on a sanitizer. Every fix in the closing pass added the check that would have caught its own defect and was mutation-tested against the pre-fix code before being accepted. Recorded as NR-547, with a proposal that verifier-headless require the mutation step for rows covering a determinism, conservation or memory-safety claim.

**One design answer came out of it** (NR-546): bit-exact conservation of a float transfer is not achievable over arbitrary weights, because `balance += amount` rounds once the destination outgrows the credit. The claim was narrowed to the half that IS exact for any inputs — the pass debits precisely what it credits — and the harness now proves the distinction with two spans that transfer a bit-identical total, one of which loses exactly zero.

Mitigated by briefing every lane to mutate what each row guards and report which mutation it ran, by requiring a sanitizer build, and by the main session re-verifying adversarially rather than trusting a self-reported green. sprints.retro:
**All three lanes merged and green; one lane's CONCLUSION was withdrawn after the merge, and that is the sprint's finding.**

What landed: BL-542's nation scorer (60/60, the first use of the 2026-08-18 grant), BL-546's migration of reputation onto the sentiment substrate with BL-391 dissolved through it (66 PASS, two save formats moved), and Sprint 28 lane A's verb-competition instrumentation (4/4). Re-verified on the integrated tree rather than on branches: nine harnesses green, zero ASan/UBSan diagnostics, warning-clean at -Wall -Wextra.

**Two lane reports did not survive verification, and neither would have been caught by reading.** A claimed layout-sensitive determinism violation in spectate does not reproduce on four clean trees, and the lane's own probe re-run moves neither hash — the likely cause, a stale object left in a rebuilt archive, bit a sibling lane in the same run and it said so. Filing it as reported would have put a false violation into the one invariant the project cannot compromise on. And a ceiling-vs-floor statistic folded its subject's WINNING scores into the ceiling, conditioning it on the outcome it explained; harmless here by luck, and fixed to the honest form.

**The bigger one came from the adversarial pass, and it invalidated the sprint's headline.** Sprint 28's finding — that Campaign's score ceiling sits below the winner's floor on exactly the silent worlds — was a two-case coincidence. At n=32 only 3 of 17 silent seeds are disjoint and 14 overlap, worst by 142 points; the diagnosis that the defect is the score LEVEL is unsupported (seed 8 clears 27,452 and fights 676 battles, seed 30 clears 2,338,095 and fights zero); and zero-war is the MODAL outcome at 53%, not a 25% pathology. What survives is the fork's answer, which is a statement about the decision rule rather than about a world: wherever a world fights nothing, Campaign clears its threshold and loses the argmax on every round.

**And underneath all of it, the instrument was measuring a sim the game does not run** — six divergences from the app's own invocation, one of which gates a whole verb out of the contest. That belongs to BL-462, which has owned it since 2026-08-18 and which this session initially duplicated as BL-554 by not searching the backlog first (NR-556).

**The method lesson, and it is N1's repeated with the stakes raised.** N1 taught that an author's own harness passes; N2 briefed every lane to mutation-test its own rows and every lane did, catching two of its own false greens before reporting. That worked. What it did not catch is the class above it: a green harness measuring the wrong fixture, and a true measurement generalised from n=2. Mutation testing proves a row has teeth against the code; it says nothing about whether the FIXTURE is the subject, or whether the SAMPLE supports the claim. Both need a different check, and the adversarial pass is what supplied it.

**Owed out of N2:** every spine still has no caller. BL-538 is the join, and it opens N3.

**POSTSCRIPT, same day.** BL-462 was fixed and the era re-measured, which supersedes both readings above. The real Era -1: **11 of 32 worlds fight nothing (34%)**, BL-384's premise is dead (2,503 battles produce 1,789 conquests), the fork answer survives on all 11 silent worlds, and **nothing separates** silent from fighting — 32 of 32 seeds overlap on the statistic that had looked decisive, and six candidate separators have now been tested and refuted. The one universal: Settle takes 83–100% of the rounds Campaign loses on every world. So three passes were needed to get one trustworthy number, and the sequence — a finding, a sample that refuted it, a fixture that refuted the sample — is the sprint's real record.
